 Neeraj Dhankher / TOI Astrology / Nov 04, 2026, 15:00 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Mercury enters Cancer on June 22, 2026, encouraging emotional clarity, intuitive decisions, meaningful conversations, and important life shifts for every zodiac sign. (AI Image) The card for 4 November is The Hermit. It stands for time alone, careful reflection and the guidance that speaks up once the world goes quiet. In the zodiac, retrograde Mercury reaches the exact heart of the Sun at around 7 PM IST. Thought and self-identity line up for a few hours. So an hour of stillness today may settle what a crowded week couldn’t. There may be a pull towards fewer people and fewer plans. It might look like hiding from things. More likely, the mind simply needs room to hear one clear thought. The Hermit Tarot Meaning for November 4 
 The Hermit: Clarity found by stepping away from the crowd. Watch One Powerful Mantra Jaap Unlock Prosperity , Wealth , Health | Prabhuji Nityanand Charandas An old man in a long grey robe stands alone on a mountaintop. In one hand he holds a lantern with a six-pointed star glowing inside. The other grips a tall staff. His light reaches only a few steps ahead. Beyond that the path is dark, and he stands there calmly anyway. This card is about taking one step, then the next. Think about what has been drowned out lately. A family group chat that buzzes all day can do it. So can an inbox checked every ten minutes. Over time the noise blurs the view of what’s actually wanted. Ten people’s advice often adds up to less than one honest hour on your own. Mercury Inside the Sun’s Glare 
 Mercury rules thought, speech and the way information travels. The Sun represents identity and purpose. When the two meet at the same degree, the mind gets lit by a stronger sense of self. Connections between ideas form more easily. Mercury is also retrograde today, and hard to see in the Sun’s glare. That fits The Hermit neatly. The best thinking happens privately, away from any audience. Write the problem down on a single page, then read it back slowly. A thought formed under this glare can feel sharp while still missing a piece. So before acting on any big conclusion, check it against one solid fact. Mute the notifications for an hour. Give that hour to one task only. How to Take a Short Retreat 
 A walk around the block without the phone counts as a retreat. So does lunch with the office door shut, or a whole evening kept free of plans. Put a time limit on it. Quiet works best when it has an edge, so it doesn’t drift into hiding from people. Come back with one written line. Either what got decided, or what’s still unclear. Both are useful. Love and Relationships 
 The Hermit: A little space may do a relationship more good than constant contact. Couples could agree on a quiet evening apart without anyone treating it as trouble. Say the reason out loud, so it isn’t mistaken for coldness. “Need a quiet night, back to normal tomorrow” clears up most worries. Singles may enjoy their own company and feel little interest in meeting anyone new. That’s perfectly fine. A message waiting for a reply can wait until tomorrow. Answer once you’re clear about what you want. Someone from the past may drift back into your thoughts. Turn it over privately first. Texts sent on a sudden urge rarely say what was meant. Career and Money 
 Today favours focused solo work. Planning and drafting go well, and so does checking figures line by line. Block two hours with no meetings and close the door if you can. If a work decision feels murky, list the facts first. Then write each option with its likely outcome beside it. The Mercury-Sun meeting rewards orderly thinking, and the answer may show up on the page itself. Avoid spending just because friends are spending. Skip online shopping meant to fill a quiet evening too. Pick one subscription and ask whether it still earns its monthly fee. That small pending bill can be paid during the same quiet hour. So, What Answer Is Waiting in the Quiet? 
 Usually the one already known underneath all the talking. The Hermit carries the lantern, and Mercury beside the Sun steadies its light. Spend one hour today making a single decision with every outside opinion switched off.
